The Guthrie Robert Packer Hospital in Sayre has been providing top-notch healthcare services to the entire northern tier of Pennsylvania for more than 130 years. In that time, they’ve continued to utilize technological advancements in the medical field to improve patient care, and I was incredibly impressed to see how they’re incorporating AI into the hospital. I enjoyed touring the facility today and appreciated the opportunity to meet with the hospital’s senior leadership. We had a great discussion about the challenges facing healthcare providers and legislation I’m working on to address issues such as nursing shortages.

The nursing workforce shortage is at a critical point and must be addressed immediately. That’s why I introduced an amendment today to increase funding for the Health Workforce Account by $10 million in the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Appropriation bill. My amendment, which is completely paid for by off-sets, will provide additional funding for Nurse Corps Programs. By expanding scholarship and loan repayment opportunities for nurses working in facilities facing shortages, we can help increase the number of health care providers in underserved communities, particularly in rural America. I am happy my amendment passed unanimously in the House and that it will be included in the final version of the bill.

I was happy to meet a group with the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists today. Doctors and medical students from across Pennsylvania’s Ninth District visited my Washington office to discuss issues related to Medicare reimbursements, maternity care services, and more.  I appreciate the organization’s efforts to advocate for improved patient care across the country, especially in rural areas.

The phase-out of the R&D Tax Credit is hitting small businesses hard, particularly those in the medical field dedicated to creating breakthrough medicines. Developing new treatments already carries a substantial price tag. Losing the ability to fully deduct their research expenses only adds more hurdles and red tape, which further strains small businesses and potentially impedes patient access to new medications and medical equipment.

During today’s @HouseSmallBiz hearing, we discussed how increased taxes and regulations have placed burdens on small businesses seeking to provide quality healthcare and treatments to their patients.

As we celebrate National Nurses Week, it's essential to recognize the profound impact nurses have on their patients and communities. They're not just caregivers; they're also advocates, leaders, and educators. So this week, thank a nurse! From Sayre, to Pottsville, to Sunbury, to Williamsport, we are so very grateful to all of the incredible nurses across Pennsylvania’s Ninth District.

Earlier today, I attended the ribbon-cutting ceremony at the Wyoming County Healthcare Center, formerly Tyler Memorial Hospital. With Guthrie now providing medical services and a full-time ambulance service, the center is fully operational, restoring vital healthcare access to Wyoming County. Thanks to Bill Ruark and his family, who purchased and revitalized the property, the Wyoming County Healthcare Center is paving the way for more accessible healthcare in the region. Supported by a $213,000 Appalachian Regional Commission (ARC) grant my office helped secure, as well as contributions from the Neighborhood Assistance Program (NAP), and the AllOne Foundation, the center is now ready to meet the healthcare needs of Wyoming County.

President @realDonaldTrump's executive order on prescription drug prices is a major step toward finally bringing fairness to American patients and taxpayers. For too long, Americans have paid far more than those in other countries for the same prescription drugs. In Europe, for example, patients often pay a tenth of what we pay here in the United States. President Trump and his Administration are taking action to change that.
 
Once again, President Trump is showing that his only special interest is the American people—and that’s mine too. By tying what we pay in the U.S. to the lowest prices paid abroad, this executive order is expected to reduce drug costs by as much as 59%. That means real relief for seniors and families across the country. 
 
This action will help increase competition and lower costs across the board for essential prescription drugs. It’s exactly the kind of bold, America-First reform we need to fix our healthcare markets—and I applaud President Trump for taking action to deliver this historic change.

In their efforts to oppose commonsense reforms to strengthen Medicaid and ensure its sustainability for the most vulnerable and future Americans, Democrats are once again resorting to fear mongering—not facts.

Below is a breakdown of common Democratic myths and the real facts about the Big Beautiful Bill (BBB) Medicaid provisions:

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

Millions will lose access to Medicaid under cruel new work requirements.

FACT:
The BBB’s Medicaid community engagement provisions apply only to able-bodied adults without dependents—not to seniors, people with disabilities, pregnant women, or caregivers.
Beginning January 1, 2026, these adults can meet the requirement by working, volunteering, attending school, or participating in job training for at least 80 hours a month.

This is not punitive—it’s empowering. It recognizes that Medicaid should support not just health but upward mobility and personal responsibility.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

Medicaid recipients will be kicked off the program due to paperwork errors and red tape.

FACT:
The BBB combats fraud, waste, and abuse, not eligible recipients.
For example, it ends the “good faith” waiver by 2030, ensuring states can no longer dodge accountability for improper payments to ineligible individuals or providers.

It uses the SSA Death Master File to prevent payments to deceased individuals and creates a federal system to prevent dual-state enrollment.

Verifying eligibility is not “red tape”—it’s responsible governance.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

The bill targets immigrants and punishes those in need.

FACT:
Federal law has long required that Medicaid recipients be citizens or legal residents.

The BBB strengthens enforcement by ending federal funding during the 90-day verification period for those without verified status.

No funding will go to those who are ineligible under federal law—this includes approximately 1.4 million illegal immigrants and 1.2 million other ineligible individuals who are currently on the rolls. 

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

States will be penalized for trying to provide compassionate care.

FACT:
Beginning in 2028, states that deliberately fund health care for undocumented immigrants through Medicaid-like programs will face a 10% reduction in federal Medicaid matching funds.

This ensures that Medicaid remains focused on U.S. citizens and legal residents—the populations it was designed to serve.

⸻

DEMOCRAT FEAR MONGERING:

These changes are meant to slash Medicaid and gut funding.

FACT:
The BBB doesn’t slash Medicaid—it strengthens it.

By removing ineligible individuals and focusing resources on those truly in need, the reforms ensure long-term sustainability of the program.

Medicaid spending is projected to grow under the BBB, not shrink, because the focus is on integrity and efficiency—not cuts.

⸻

Bottom Line:
The BBB reforms don’t weaken Medicaid—they preserve it for those who need it most: vulnerable seniors, low-income children, people with disabilities, and legal working families.

Democrats are trying to protect bureaucracy. Republicans are fighting to protect people.

This morning on @Varneyco, I discussed Democrats' fear-mongering on common sense Medicaid reform.  

The Big Beautiful Bill saves money for American families while strengthening Medicaid for our most vulnerable—seniors, children, people with disabilities, and legal residents—by ensuring no funds go to ineligible recipients.  

President Trump's plan to lower perscription drug costs could also save an additional $1 trillion over the next decade.  

The BBB provides a solid framework, but we must continue to build on this important first step.

This morning, I spoke on the House floor in strong support of the FY26 MilCon-VA Appropriations Act—a significant investment in our veterans, military families, and national security.

The bill:

• Fully funds veterans' medical care—$131B
• Invests in military family housing and Guard facilities
• Supports President Trump’s effort to end veteran homelessness
• Protects Second Amendment rights for veterans

This bill will directly benefit the 45,000 veterans in our District, as well as their families. I urge my colleagues to pass this legislation, which reflects our values, strengthens our defense, and ensures we never waver in our duty to those who’ve sacrificed for our freedom.

Despite the media’s falsehoods and Democrat fearmongering, eligible American citizens will not lose Medicaid coverage under the One Big Beautiful Bill.
 
This legislation strengthens Medicaid for those who are eligible under the law by rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse—not by targeting the vulnerable. In fact, Medicaid spending has increased 57% over the last five years, underscoring the urgent need for responsible reforms that protect the program’s future.
 
Here are the facts, the only individuals affected by these reforms are those who do not meet eligibility or participation standards:
 
▪️ Able-bodied adults without dependents who choose not to meet modest 20-hour-per-week work, education, or service requirements

▪️ Illegal immigrants who were never eligible in the first place

▪️ Ineligible individuals improperly kept on the rolls under Biden-era policies
 
Republicans are restoring integrity to the program and protecting Medicaid for seniors, the disabled, and low-income families who rely on it.
